thread:
oliver: hey team, new hire question. I'm running a nightly batch to build embeddings from an internal docs dump (~80k files, ~1.2M tokens). Using my hosted sandbox key and kept hitting 429s midway through. error message:
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
x-ratelimit-type: token
retry-after: 45
```
Anyone know the quickest path to get a short bump or alternative so the nightly job can finish? I don't need production access, just a one-off increase or a scheduled reserved run.

infra-bot: Note: sandbox keys have conservative quotas. For temporary increases email infra@redwood.com with subject "sandbox-temp" and include account id, token id (if available), total tokens, peak qps, and desired window. Auto-approve common for <= 5M tokens and <= 4h.

maria: @oliver you can also split the run into small batches with a backoff and checkpointing, then resume after retry. We use that pattern in eng experiments to avoid quota spikes.

jon: If you prefer ops to run it, we have a reserved batch window Saturdays 02:00-05:00 UTC. Upload sanitized data to internal tmp S3 and ping me the path; ops can execute the job from a dedicated account that doesn't consume your sandbox bucket quota.

security-lee: quick reminder: make sure the S3 object has proper ACLs and that any customer PII is redacted. Mark the object with tag "sensitive:yes" only if it's still sensitive; otherwise tag "sensitive:no".

oliver: thanks. I'd rather not re-architect the pipeline yet. Jon, can I get the Saturday slot? I'll sanitize and upload tonight. Ops, cost center is "infra-eval" and estimated total tokens ~1.2M, burst ~10 qps.

ops-nora: Roger. Jon and I will coordinate. Please upload the S3 path and set lifecycle to 7 days. We'll run it in the 02:00-05:00 UTC window and post completion here.

oliver: Uploaded and shared the S3 path in a DM to Jon. Appreciate the help :pray:
